species.identification:
Warty Skin
Trunkated finger and toe tips
Golden iris interspersed with black lines
species.habitat: Arboreal: On trees branching along stream sides in moist-evergreen to deciduous forest.

species.identification:
Extremely small; males are 22–24 mm, while females are slightly larger at 28–33 mm.
Stream-lined body with pointed snout.
species.habitat: Fast-flowing streams in primary and secondary forests.

species.identification: Horizontal pupil; Wrinkled dorsum; Subocular gland is prominent
species.habitat: In water streams, stream edges, in evergreen moist deciduous forest, roadside streams

species.identification: Blue ring around the eye; small frog, males measuring 24–29 mm ; The dominant colour form is yellowish brown with light-brownish lines or light-yellowish with discontinuous light-brown lines
species.habitat: Arboreal: Bushes, commonly found in disturbed habitats, near coffee plantations adjacent to primary forests and waysides.

species.identification: Reddish brown Iris; Large Tympanum; Strong fold from eye to shoulder; Back yellow, sides brown
species.habitat: On land- forest floor, leaf litter, tree base, stream sides, dam backwaters

species.identification:
Medium-sized leaping frogs endemic to the Western Ghats. 
The hind-limbs have reduced webbing compared to its congeners.
They have a prominent tympanum.
They have semi-terrestrial tadpoles.
species.habitat: Leaf litter and Rocky surfaces often with film of water.

species.authority: Sanchez, Biju, Islam, Hasan, Ohler, Vences, and Kurabayashi, 2018
species.identification:
Minervarya sahyadris is a small-sized frog endemic to the Western Ghats of India.
This species is about 22 mm in length and is nocturnal.
They have a pointed snout and a supratympanic fold from back of eye to shoulder
species.habitat: Open terrestrial habitats; breeds around puddles
